etymologies.etymologyHTML: Variant of earlier out-fit, from fit out. Equivalent to out- +‎ fit.

quote.text: Don't call what you're wearing an outfit.

definitions.definition: Gear consisting of a set of articles or tools for a specified purpose.
Any cohesive group of people; a unit; such as a military company.

quote.citation: 2008, BioWare, Mass Effect, Redwood City: Electronic Arts, →ISBN, →OCLC, PC, scene: Salarians: League of One Codex entry:
quote.text: The League of One was suddenly exposed and in danger of being hunted by enemies of the salarians. Before any harm could be done, the team mysteriously disappeared.[...]Realizing the threat posed by this rogue outfit, the Special Tasks Group dispatched a team of hunters. When they didn't return, the STG dispatched ten of its brightest operators with broad discretionary powers. Only two returned; they reported no evidence of the League.

quote.citation: 2011 October 20, Jamie Lillywhite, “Tottenham 1 - 0 Rubin Kazan”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: With only two fit centre-backs available, Tottenham boss Harry Redknapp employed young midfielder Jake Livermore at the back alongside Sebastien Bassong but Spurs struggled against a seasoned Champions League outfit, who beat Barcelona at the Nou Camp in 2009-10 and continually worked their way between the home defence to create some golden opportunities.

definitions.definition: (Canada, historical) A fiscal year of the Hudson's Bay Company, or the supplies required for such a period.

quote.citation: 1949, John McLoughlin, The Financial Papers of Dr. John McLoughlin, page 56:
quote.text: […]  the outfit of 1821, which outfit suffered a loss. From 1822 there were profits on each outfit as the many subsequent credit entries indicate.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To provide with, usually for a specific purpose.
